variants.headline: Business-start grant programme ends
variants.sub: Business-starting support under {programme} has come to an end.
variants.body:
The programme {programme} has ended, having paid {paid} grants and refused {refused} applications. It supported people starting a business. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that record from a judgment that either the existence or the end of a programme proves it served its purpose adequately.

Payments and refusals describe the programme's reach, not a return on investment by themselves. Commercial readers should distinguish an allocation record from the performance of businesses receiving support. The useful assessment asks what the scheme achieved without presuming that every grant was a success or every refusal a mistake.

We criticise {target} on the standard of public support. A programme's ending should not put its stewardship beyond question or allow its attractive purpose to stand in for a serious account of performance. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
